contract.window_ledger: best-effort; swallows; never blocks a trading path. UNCHANGED
contract.order_journal: fail-closed; raises; a write that did not land must stop the order
contract.why: a failed write in the ledger would let an order go out with no record of intent — the one thing a write-ahead log exists to prevent

design_hole_found_by_a_failing_test.what: Stage 5U said SUBMITTED meant 'handed to the broker', which never said whether the line is written before or after the call
design_hole_found_by_a_failing_test.the_hole: if written after, a process dying inside send_order would leave a journal whose last state is INTENDED while a live order existed — and INTENDED is documented as 'nothing was sent'
design_hole_found_by_a_failing_test.resolution: SUBMITTED is written BEFORE send_order is called; the same discipline track1_switch already follows ('Every stage emits BEFORE it acts')
design_hole_found_by_a_failing_test.cost: the opposite error, and the cheap one: an order that was never sent looks unresolved until a reconcile says the broker has nothing
design_hole_found_by_a_failing_test.consequence: INTENDED is genuinely safe to read as 'the broker was never reached' and is not in UNRESOLVED
design_hole_found_by_a_failing_test.found_by: my own test expecting both INTENDED and SUBMITTED to count as unresolved; it failed and being wrong about it exposed the ambiguity

corruption_handling.corrupt_line: returned by read() as an invalid entry with file and line number — never dropped
corruption_handling.impossible_history_on_disk: resolve() raises rather than repairing — a reader that quietly fixes the journal is a reader that can be lied to
